environment.externalLoad: Four unrelated long-running processes remained confined primarily to CPUs 12-15. Scaling used the full 0-15 allowance with paired 8/12/15 plateau measurement; accepted incremental and large-corpus measurements used CPUs 0-11. The first determinism attempt requested worker 15 under a 0-11 affinity mask and was rejected by the product. Two incremental confirmations failed the frozen variance gate under transient host contention and filesystem-cache warm-up. All complete failed roots remain excluded; the full-affinity determinism retry and 1.54%-CoV incremental retry are the accepted evidence.

excludedEvidence.reason: Excluded complete retry: transient host contention raised incremental wall-time CoV to 20.49%, above the frozen 10% gate.
Excluded complete retry: two transient host-contention samples raised large first-import wall-time CoV to 42.07%, above the frozen 10% gate.

conclusions.branchReason: Both decision composites exceed the 4x/750ms warm-benefit rule while first import, RSS, store allocation, startup, recovery, privacy, incremental-work, and equality gates pass.
conclusions.throughputPlateau: In the paired 8/12/15 decision run, 12 workers are the fastest stable point and are 0.54% ahead of 15; 8 is 6.24% slower than the fastest point and outside the 2% band, so 12 remains the smallest point within 2% of the fastest stable median.
conclusions.utilizationDisposition: Primary and confirmation large-corpus runs retain the original 30-second/80% outcomes as false. Under the user-approved amendment, stable near-fastest throughput and RSS are the blocking performance criteria.
conclusions.coldDefinition: First traversal of a newly materialized synthetic corpus or a fresh store; privileged page-cache eviction was unavailable, so filesystem cache state is disclosed rather than labeled physically cold.
